title: Sudden CEO death and firm value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology using the market model. The key assumption is that in the absence of the CEO death event, stock returns would have followed their normal relationship with market returns as established in the estimation window. We estimate normal performance using the market model over the estimation window [-10,-2], then calculate abnormal returns as the difference between actual and expected returns during the event window [0,+1].

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s12_data.csv")

# Step 1: Estimate market model parameters for each firm using estimation window [-10, -2]
estimation_data <- data %>% 
  filter(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2)

# Calculate market model parameters (alpha and beta) for each firm
market_model_params <- estimation_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do(model = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    alpha = coef(model)[1],
    beta_est = coef(model)[2]
  ) %>%
  select(stock_id, alpha, beta_est)

# Step 2: Calculate abnormal returns for event window [0, +1]
event_data <- data %>% 
  filter(event_day >= 0 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  left_join(market_model_params, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    expected_ret = alpha + beta_est * mkt_ret,
    abnormal_ret = ret - expected_ret
  )

# Step 3: Calculate Cumulative Abnormal Returns (CAR) for each firm
car_by_firm <- event_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_01 = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Test statistical significance
# Calculate average CAR across all firms
avg_car <- mean(car_by_firm$CAR_01)
n_firms <- nrow(car_by_firm)

# Calculate standard error and t-statistic
se_car <- sd(car_by_firm$CAR_01) / sqrt(n_firms)
t_stat <- avg_car / se_car
p_value <- 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = n_firms - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Print main results
cat("=== EVENT STUDY RESULTS ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of firms: %d\n", n_firms))
cat(sprintf("Average CAR [0,+1]: %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", avg_car, avg_car * 100))
cat(sprintf("Standard Error: %.4f\n", se_car))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic: %.4f\n", t_stat))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", p_value))
cat(sprintf("95%% Confidence Interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", 
    avg_car - 1.96 * se_car, avg_car + 1.96 * se_car))

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Check individual event days
daily_abnormal <- event_data %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(avg_abnormal_ret = mean(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop')

cat("Daily average abnormal returns:\n")
for(i in 1:nrow(daily_abnormal)) {
  day <- daily_abnormal$event_day[i]
  ret <- daily_abnormal$avg_abnormal_ret[i]
  cat(sprintf("Day %d: %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", day, ret, ret * 100))
}

# 2. Sign test (proportion of negative CARs)
negative_cars <- sum(car_by_firm$CAR_01 < 0)
prop_negative <- negative_cars / n_firms
cat(sprintf("\nSign test: %d out of %d firms (%.1f%%) have negative CAR\n", 
    negative_cars, n_firms, prop_negative * 100))

# 3. Median CAR
median_car <- median(car_by_firm$CAR_01)
cat(sprintf("Median CAR [0,+1]: %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", median_car, median_car * 100))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a significantly negative CAR in the range of -3% to -8% over the [0,+1] window. The sudden death of a CEO represents a major negative shock to firm value due to: (1) loss of firm-specific human capital and leadership, (2) increased uncertainty about future strategic direction, (3) potential succession concerns, and (4) disruption to ongoing operations and relationships. The magnitude should be economically significant since CEO death is an unexpected, permanent shock, unlike temporary events. The effect should be most pronounced on day 0 (announcement day) with possible continuation into day +1 as markets fully process the implications.

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms experience significant negative CAR on CEO death announcement
